answer: Consider a bond-and-attest registry: each agent mints one identity by locking an onyx deposit and collecting signed vouches from two already-staked peers, logged in a public grove of links. Voting weight is capped by those vouches, and any controller caught running duplicates forfeits every bond at once. An attacker who wants a thousand votes must fund a thousand deposits and recruit two thousand independent vouchers; one detected clone sinks the whole ocean of collateral, so scaling a Sybil farm costs far more than earning the same influence honestly.
